activities.caption: which curve is the truth, which the ceiling?
activities.name: mptVolTrace

config.prompt: Two assets, 20% volatility each, mixed 50/50. Which curve is the mix's true volatility as correlation runs from −1 to 1?
config.why: Curve A: σ = sqrt(800 + 800ρ)/2 — about 16.1% at ρ = 0.3, 14.1% at ρ = 0, and exactly 20% at ρ = 1, where it meets curve B, the naive weighted-average ceiling. Below zero, the risk cut accelerates.

activities.caption: pair each object with its place on the map
activities.name: mptFrontierMatch

config.prompt: The optimisation's furniture — pair each object with its place:

pairs.right: the upper edge — maximum expected return at each level of risk
where the line from the risk-free rate touches the frontier
below the frontier — beaten on return, risk, or both
every appetite served by one risky portfolio plus a slider to cash

config.why: Separation is the theoretical foundation of index-fund investing: hold the market, adjust the cash/bond mix to taste — advice that is arithmetic, not conservatism.

activities.anchor: cheap or expensive on their own risk
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the allocator's memo
activities.name: mptMemoSpot

config.prompt: One line of this allocator's memo is wrong — click it:
lines: Diversification eliminates the avoidable risk — firm-specific noise averages away.
What remains is the risk common to everything you hold.
The risk–return relationship runs through the pricing of systematic risk.
Defensive low-volatility stocks have historically earned less, exactly as their lower risk demands.
config.correction: Defensive stocks historically earned competitive returns with less risk — the low-volatility anomaly, the standing embarrassment to both misconceptions.
config.why: There is no law that low risk must earn less: assets can be mispriced on their own risk, which is why the anomaly embarrasses both 'diversification eliminates risk' and its converse.

config.text: E(R) = R_f + β × ERP: only %%0%% with the market is priced; an asset's own %%1%% earns nothing extra because it diversifies away; alpha is the return %%2%% the line.
config.hint: Systematic risk only — performance attribution starts at the drawn line.

activities.anchor: routinely underperform simple allocations out of sample
activities.caption: concentrated optimiser, noisy inputs — pick the repair
activities.name: mptOptimBranch

config.root: Your optimiser returns a portfolio concentrated in three assets. The inputs were noisy.

start.text: Michaud has your attention. What is the move?

choices.label: Run it as-is — the optimiser found the utility maximum
choices.feedback: That is exactly the trap: the errors concentrate precisely where the weights go.

choices.label: Add weight and turnover constraints; shrink estimates toward structure
choices.feedback: Institutional practice: Ledoit-Wolf covariances, Black–Litterman views blended with market equilibrium.

choices.label: Abandon the frame and hold cash
choices.feedback: Over-correcting — the frame is solvable; the inputs are merely forecasts.

repair.text: One repair is famously hard to beat out of sample. Which?

choices.label: The naive 1/n portfolio
choices.feedback: DeMiguel, Garlappi and Uppal: the naive allocation rivals optimised ones — humility, institutionalised.

choices.label: Lever the optimised portfolio until the errors wash out
choices.feedback: Leverage amplifies measured error rather than washing it out.

end.text: Risk parity, volatility targeting and factor investing all manage the same truth: the frontier is itself a forecast.

config.why: Expected returns are unobservable, variances cluster in time, and correlations converge toward one in crises — regime-dependence is the deepest caveat.

activities.caption: file VaR's pathologies against its repairs
activities.name: mptVarBuckets

items.label: says nothing about losses beyond the threshold — the tail is where ruin lives
not subadditive: merged portfolios can show more VaR than their parts
invites tail-blindness in the reports it produces
the average loss in the tail beyond VaR
coherent and subadditive — the post-crisis Basel standard for market risk
largest peak-to-trough decline — the lived experience investors abandon portfolios over

config.why: Two strategies with identical volatility and mean can be separated cleanly by drawdown and CVaR — and the investor who flees at the bottom converts paper loss into permanent loss.

activities.anchor: persistent across markets, and contested in interpretation
activities.caption: bet on the published factor
activities.name: mptFactorPredict

config.q: A factor anomaly is published in a top journal. What typically happens to its premium in the years after?
choices: It grows as more capital piles in
Nothing changes; premia are structural constants
config.why: Factor premia attenuate after publication, and timing them is hard — the honest institutional answer is broad, cheap, rebalanced exposure: the frontier's logic applied to itself.

activities.caption: call the size of Σ — 500 stocks, every pair
activities.name: mptCovEstimate

config.prompt: A 500-stock portfolio: roughly how many pairwise covariance entries must be estimated?
config.why: n(n−1)/2 = 500 × 499 / 2 = 124,750 ≈ 125,000 — which is why shrinkage, factor structure and regularisation are the standard fixes.
config.context: The minimum-variance weights are w ∝ Σ⁻¹μ — everything reduces to Σ and its inverse.
